metric.why: Liquid-cooled AI racks with coolant, manifolds, and batteries are dramatically heavier than the enterprise racks most buildings were engineered for. Retrofit projects hit structural limits before electrical ones more often than the industry expected.
metric.definition: The structural weight the raised floor or slab supports per square foot, against the actual weight of installed racks.

reading.body:
Structural floor capacity, not electrical capacity, is the first hard limit that retrofit data centers hit when liquid-cooled AI racks are installed.

Floor loading is the structural weight a raised floor or slab supports per square foot, set against the weight of the racks actually installed. Liquid-cooled AI racks carry coolant, manifolds, and batteries, which makes them far heavier than the enterprise racks most buildings were engineered for. Retrofit projects reach structural limits before electrical ones more often than the industry expected.

For AI, this moves the binding constraint inside the building. A site can have power contracted and cooling designed and still be unable to carry the load on its floor. The shell becomes part of the limit on where AI capacity can be added, alongside the supply feeding it.

The data does not quantify any of this. There are no weight thresholds, no per-square-foot ratings, no count of affected sites, and no cost or schedule for structural remediation. It also does not separate new builds from retrofits, or say how often the structural limit is the one that stops a project. It is a definition and a directional claim, not a measurement.
